सिनेमाघरों में गदर मचाने आ गई है Ramayana, और सेट से आई है सबसे क्यूट तस्वीर! ✨

3 साल के लंबे इंतजार के बाद Nitesh Tiwari के डायरेक्शन में बनी film गुरुवार को सिनेमाघरों में रिलीज हो चुकी है।
रिपोर्ट्स के मुताबिक, Part 2 को मिलाकर इस film का कुल बजट ₹ 4000 crores बताया जा रहा है।
film में Ranbir Kapoor ने Ram, Sai Pallavi ने Sita, Ravie Dubey ने Laxman और Yash ने Raavan का किरदार निभाया है।
Alia Bhatt जब बेटी Raha को लेकर सेट पर पहुंचीं, तो फाइट सीक्वेंस की शूटिंग के बीच Ranbir डैडी ड्यूटी निभाते नजर आए।
Alia ने बेहद प्यार जताते हुए लिखा, "you poured everything into this one... so proud of you Ranbir", और पूरी टीम की तारीफ की। ❤️

क्या आपने सिनेमाघरों में यह film देख ली है? कमेंट्स में अपनी राय जरूर बताएं! 💬

ctx.title: Alia Bhatt shares the cutest BTS pictures of Ranbir with Raha on Ramayana sets: ‘So proud of you…’
ctx.summary: Alia Bhatt has shared adorable pics of hubby Ranbir Kapoor and daughter
ctx.text:
Ramayana Rise of a Legend has finally seen the light of day. In the making for three years now, the hype was truly building up over time, and reached its crescendo upon its release in theatres on Thursday.
Alia Bhatt has now shared a glimpse of what went down behind the scenes, on the sets, when she took daughter Raha for a visit. Ranbir Kapoor , seemingly shooting for a fight sequence, took out time for his daddy duties. Check out the cute moments:
Alia wrote in the caption, “you poured everything into this one and somehow still had all of it left for her, so proud of you Ranbir and of every single person who brought their heart and soul to this incredible experience at the movies. Some stories are bigger than all of us & Ramayana is one of them”
Ramayana, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, has been reportedly mounted on a budget of ₹ 4000 crores, which includes Part Two as well. Starring Ranbir as Ram, Sai pallavi as Sita, Ravie Dubey as Laxman, and Yash as Raavan, it has opened to positive reviews. HT's review of Ramayana says, “…all that money shows on screen. This is not an average VFX driven film; care has actually been put into how it all looks. Ramayana Part 1 can truly stand up to any Hollywood film in this aspect. What is also praiseworthy is how care has been taken to cover the basics properly: from how Raavan took over Kuber's Lanka, his Shiv bhakti, that moment of horror when Kaikayi realises her folly in sending Ram for van-vaas… all this sucks you into the film. The makers have not messed with how Indians remember the story.”
